I am an NLP research group lead and I need to set up a research tracker for recent papers on efficient transformer architectures, including topics like flash attention, token merging and pruning, low-rank adaptation, quantization-aware training, and sparse mixture of experts. The database contains exactly five papers relevant to these topics, along with some unrelated papers on other subjects. Include exactly the five relevant papers and do not add any others.

For each paper, please search the arxiv database for papers related to efficient transformers and model compression. Look for papers whose titles or abstracts mention topics such as attention efficiency, token merging, LoRA, quantization, or mixture of experts in the context of transformers. The five relevant papers cover exactly these topics: (1) attention efficiency / flash attention, (2) token merging and pruning, (3) low-rank adaptation (LoRA), (4) quantization-aware training, and (5) sparse mixture of experts. Exclude papers that do not fit this efficient-transformer theme, such as robotics or drone navigation and molecular property prediction papers, even if they appear in the search results. Then for each paper you find, look up its citation count and publication venue information through a scholarly search. Cross-reference by title to get accurate citation metrics. Note: the arXiv search tools do not return citation counts or publication venues, so you must obtain those from the scholarly search tools, matching each paper by its title.

Once you have gathered all the information, create an Excel file called Transformer_Research_Tracker.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets.

The first sheet should be named "Paper Comparison" and should have the following columns: Paper_ID, Title, Authors, Published_Date, Venue, Citation_Count, Primary_Category, Key_Contribution. Each row should represent one of the relevant papers. The Key_Contribution column should contain a brief one-sentence summary of each paper's main contribution. Sort the papers by Citation_Count in descending order.

The second sheet should be named "Statistics" and should have two columns: Metric and Value. Include the following metrics: Total_Papers (the number of papers tracked), Avg_Citations (the average citation count across all tracked papers rounded to one decimal place), Most_Cited_Paper (the title of the paper with the highest citation count), Top_Venue (the venue that appears most frequently among the tracked papers), and Date_Range (the range of publication dates in the format "YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD").

Finally, create a page in the team knowledge base titled "Efficient Transformers Research Tracker" that provides a structured overview of the research landscape. The page should include a heading or introduction summarizing the research area, a section listing each paper with its title, authors, citation count, and a brief description, a section with key observations or trends across the papers, and information about the most impactful papers and common themes.

Please complete all steps and save the Excel file to the workspace. Make sure the knowledge base page has substantive content that would be useful for tracking research progress.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, follow this exact orchestration plan. A wave must finish and return all stated handoffs before the next wave begins. Within a wave, dispatch exactly one sub-agent for each numbered sub-task and run those sub-agents concurrently.

Before Wave 1, the main agent must freeze exactly the five task-defined topic slots—flash/efficient attention, token merging or pruning, LoRA, quantization-aware training, and sparse mixture of experts—and the exclusion rule for robotics, navigation, molecules, and other unrelated work. It must assign one topic per agent without assuming paper identities or source values.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 5 sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

   1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): Use one explore sub-agent to research attention efficiency or flash attention.
   2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 1): Use one explore sub-agent to research token merging and pruning.
   3. explore 2 (academic-literature-researcher 2): Use one explore sub-agent to research low-rank adaptation.
   4. explore 3 (academic-literature-researcher 3): Use one explore sub-agent to research quantization-aware training.
   5. explore 4 (academic-literature-researcher 4): Use one explore sub-agent to research sparse mixture of experts.

Each Wave 1 sub-agent must search arXiv and Scholarly read-only for only its assigned topic, validate relevance from title/abstract, cross-reference venue and numeric citation count by title, and return the strongest source-backed paper matching that slot as one compact record containing stable ID, title, full authors, published date, venue, numeric citation count, primary category, one-sentence contribution, search controls, provenance, and missing/conflict status. Explore is read-only, so do not write files or create Excel or Notion state, and do not retain an unrelated paper merely to fill a slot.

After Wave 1, the main agent must verify exactly one distinct relevant paper per supported topic, resolve duplicates and source conflicts, sort the frozen five-paper set by citation count, and compute literal statistics only from that set.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own Transformer_Research_Tracker.xlsx exclusively. Create exactly Paper Comparison and Statistics with the exact headers/metrics, five citation-descending rows, literal numeric counts and one-decimal average, correctly resolved most-cited paper, runtime top venue, and date range. Read back both sheets and return path, row/metric controls, sort order, and validation. Do not modify Notion.

   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own the single Notion page exclusively. Search for Efficient Transformers Research Tracker, create at most one page, and add a substantive overview, one source-backed section per frozen paper with authors/citations/contribution, cross-paper trends, impactful papers, and common themes. Read it back and return page ID/title, five-paper/section coverage, and validation. Do not write the workbook.

After Wave 2, the main agent must reconcile all five IDs, citations, venues, contributions, statistics, and exclusions across workbook and page and verify both external state and file integrity before completion.

You are an academic literature researcher for an NLP research group building a tracker on efficient transformer architectures. Your assigned topic slot is: **attention efficiency / flash attention** (efficient attention mechanisms, flash attention, linear attention, sparse attention, etc., in transformers).

CONTEXT: The group maintains a database of exactly five relevant papers (one per topic slot: attention efficiency, token merging/pruning, LoRA, quantization-aware training, sparse MoE). Unrelated papers (robotics/drone navigation, molecular property prediction, or anything not fitting the efficient-transformer theme) must be EXCLUDED even if they appear in search results. Your job is to find the single strongest, source-backed paper matching YOUR topic slot only.

STEPS:
1. Use mcp__arxiv_local__search_papers with queries such as: "flash attention", "efficient attention" OR "attention efficiency", ti:"flash attention", with categories like ["cs.LG", "cs.CL", "cs.AI"] — use a few query variants to find the most relevant candidate(s). You may use mcp__arxiv_local__download_paper and mcp__arxiv_local__read_paper to verify title/abstract relevance for candidates.
2. Use mcp__scholarly__search-google-scholar and/or mcp__scholarly__search-arxiv with the exact paper title to look up the NUMERIC CITATION COUNT and PUBLICATION VENUE (journal/conference, e.g. NeurIPS/ICML/ACL). Cross-reference by title to get accurate citation metrics. If Google Scholar gives a citation count, use it; record provenance of the number.
3. Verify the paper's relevance from title/abstract: it must be about attention efficiency / flash attention in transformers.

- published_date: YYYY-MM-DD (from arXiv)

You are an office-report builder. Build an Excel workbook **Transformer_Research_Tracker.xlsx** in the workspace directory: `/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-research-tracker-notion/workspace/Transformer_Research_Tracker.xlsx` (use the mcp__excel__ tools; create_workbook with that full filepath). Use this FROZEN, verified five-paper dataset (already cross-referenced by title against arXiv + Google Scholar by the research team). Do not add, remove, or rename any paper.

The five papers, sorted by Citation_Count DESCENDING (this exact order must be preserved in the sheet):

Row 1 (most cited):
- Paper_ID: 2402.10003
- Title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
- Authors: Edward Hu, Yelong Shen
- Published_Date: 2024-02-20
- Venue: ICLR
- Citation_Count: 1200
- Primary_Category: cs.CL
- Key_Contribution: Introduces low-rank adaptation (LoRA) that freezes pre-trained weights and injects trainable low-rank decomposition matrices, cutting trainable parameters 10,000x for GPT-3 175B with no added inference latency.

Row 2:
- Paper_ID: 2402.10001
- Title: FlashAttention-3: Fast and Memory-Efficient Attention with IO-Awareness
- Authors: Tri Dao, Daniel Fu
- Published_Date: 2024-02-15
- Venue: NeurIPS
- Citation_Count: 520
- Primary_Category: cs.LG
- Key_Contribution: Extends IO-aware exact attention with asynchronous block-wise computation and improved SRAM/HBM tiling, achieving a 2.1x speedup over FlashAttention-2 and linear-memory training for sequences up to 128K tokens.

Row 3:
- Paper_ID: 2402.10005
- Title: Sparse Mixture of Experts for Scalable Transformer Models
- Authors: William Fedus, Jeff Dean
- Published_Date: 2024-02-25
- Venue: JMLR
- Citation_Count: 340
- Primary_Category: cs.AI
- Key_Contribution: Replaces dense FFN layers with sparsely-activated expert layers routed by a learned gating mechanism, matching a dense model's perplexity at 4x its compute while scaling capacity 8-64x.

Row 4:
- Paper_ID: 2402.10002
- Title: Efficient Transformers via Token Merging and Pruning
- Authors: Daniel Bolya, Cheng-Yang Fu
- Published_Date: 2024-02-18
- Venue: ICLR
- Citation_Count: 180
- Primary_Category: cs.CV
- Key_Contribution: A unified, retraining-free framework that merges similar tokens and prunes uninformative ones via bipartite matching, cutting token count up to 60% within 0.3% of ImageNet accuracy.

Row 5 (least cited):
- Paper_ID: 2402.10004
- Title: Quantization-Aware Training for Efficient Transformer Inference
- Authors: Jianlin Su, Minjia Zhang
- Published_Date: 2024-02-22
- Venue: ICML
- Citation_Count: 95
- Primary_Category: cs.LG
- Key_Contribution: A QAT framework with learnable quantization step sizes and mixed-precision quantization (4-bit FFN weights, 8-bit attention activations) reaching within 0.5 perplexity of full precision while shrinking model size 4x.

- Sheet 1 named "Paper Comparison": columns exactly: Paper_ID | Title | Authors | Published_Date | Venue | Citation_Count | Primary_Category | Key_Contribution. Header in row 1, then the 5 data rows in the order above (Citation_Count descending: 1200, 520, 340, 180, 95). Citation_Count must be stored as numeric values (1200, 520, 340, 180, 95), Published_Date as YYYY-MM-DD strings.

  - Date_Range | 2024-02-15 to 2024-02-25   (min to max published date across the five papers)

You are an external-workflow operator for a team knowledge base. Create ONE Notion page titled **"Efficient Transformers Research Tracker"** using the mcp__notion__ tools. Do NOT write or modify any Excel files.

STEPS:
1. Search Notion (mcp__notion__API-post-search with query "Efficient Transformers Research Tracker") to check whether a page with this title already exists. If it already exists, do NOT create a duplicate — reuse/update that page. If it does not exist, create exactly one page via mcp__notion__API-post-page (parent: use the top-level page returned by search of an existing parent page if available; otherwise create with workspace parent if supported — prefer a parent page found via API-post-search with an empty or broad query if needed). Title must be exactly "Efficient Transformers Research Tracker".
2. Populate the page with substantive content using mcp__notion__API-patch-block-children (append blocks). Include:
   - A heading_1 or heading_2 introduction/overview summarizing the research area: efficient transformer architectures spanning attention efficiency (FlashAttention), token merging/pruning, low-rank adaptation (LoRA), quantization-aware training, and sparse mixture of experts — the goal of tracking recent advances for the NLP research group.
   - A section "Papers Tracked" (heading_2) with ONE bulleted_list_item (or paragraph per paper) for EACH of the five papers below, each including: title, authors, citation count, and a brief description (the key contribution).
   - A heading_2 section "Key Observations and Trends" with 3-5 bullet points of cross-paper trends (e.g., all five papers are from Feb 2024; efficiency gains come from reducing compute/memory/parameters at different layers of the stack — attention (FlashAttention-3), tokens (merging/pruning), parameters (LoRA, sparse MoE), and numerical precision (QAT); methods are complementary — token merging complements quantization/KD; sparse MoE trades capacity for constant per-token compute; ICLR hosts two of the five papers, etc.).
   - A heading_2 section "Most Impactful Papers and Common Themes" covering: the most impactful paper (LoRA with 1200 citations; FlashAttention-3 with 520; Sparse MoE with 340), and common themes (retaining model quality while reducing cost, retraining-free or minimal-training approaches, IO/memory awareness, and conditional/low-precision computation).

THE FROZEN FIVE PAPERS (exact data — use as-is, citation counts are numeric from Google Scholar):
1. LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models — Edward Hu, Yelong Shen — 1200 citations — Introduces low-rank adaptation (LoRA) freezing pre-trained weights and injecting trainable low-rank matrices, cutting trainable parameters 10,000x for GPT-3 175B with no inference latency. (ICLR)
2. FlashAttention-3: Fast and Memory-Efficient Attention with IO-Awareness — Tri Dao, Daniel Fu — 520 citations — IO-aware exact attention with asynchronous block-wise computation, 2.1x faster than FlashAttention-2 on A100, linear-memory training up to 128K-token sequences. (NeurIPS)
3. Sparse Mixture of Experts for Scalable Transformer Models — William Fedus, Jeff Dean — 340 citations — Sparse MoE replacing dense FFNs with gated expert layers plus load-balancing, matching dense perplexity at 4x compute while scaling capacity 8-64x. (JMLR)
4. Efficient Transformers via Token Merging and Pruning — Daniel Bolya, Cheng-Yang Fu — 180 citations — Retraining-free framework merging similar tokens and pruning uninformative ones via bipartite matching, cutting tokens up to 60% within 0.3% of ImageNet accuracy. (ICLR)
5. Quantization-Aware Training for Efficient Transformer Inference — Jianlin Su, Minjia Zhang — 95 citations — QAT with learnable step sizes and mixed precision (4-bit FFN weights, 8-bit attention activations), within 0.5 perplexity of full precision with 4x smaller models. (ICML)

VERIFICATION (mandatory): After creating/populating, retrieve the page (mcp__notion__API-retrieve-a-page) and read back its block children (mcp__notion__API-get-block-children) to confirm the title and that all five papers plus the overview/trends/impact sections are present.
